position: Eliminate politicization, reestablish trust and accountability, and restore faith to the force
proposal: The Mandate recommends strengthening protections for military chaplains to minister according to the tenets of their faith. It also recommends codifying language telling three- and four-star officers that their primary duty is readiness rather than a social engineering agenda, reinforced in Senate confirmations, with purely partisan orders identified as threats to readiness.

status_summary: In December 2025 the Secretary of War issued a directive on the Chaplain Corps that eliminated the Army spiritual fitness guide effective 2025-12-16, began streamlining the faith coding system and described chaplains as moral anchors rather than emotional support, according to a Center Square report; the Justice Department welcomed the action on 2025-12-17. H.R. 8769, the Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026, was introduced on 2026-05-12 and referred to the House Armed Services Committee, and a Senate version introduced on 2026-08-06 would let chaplains minister according to their beliefs and bar retaliatory personnel actions; the senator's release says the bill is included in the House-passed FY2027 NDAA. No statute, directive or confirmation requirement using the Mandate's senior-officer readiness language was found.

timeline.event: A Secretary of War directive on the Chaplain Corps took effect, eliminating the Army spiritual fitness guide and streamlining faith and belief coding (date inferred from a report of 2025-12-18 saying the guide's elimination was effective Tuesday).
H.R. 8769, the Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026, was introduced and referred to the House Armed Services Committee.
A Senate version of the Military Chaplains Modernization Act was introduced, setting chaplain duties, protecting ministry according to beliefs and barring retaliatory personnel actions.

title: Protect chaplains' ministry and codify senior officers' readiness duty
uncertainties: The December 2025 directive was not read; its content comes from a Center Square report, and the Justice Department statement does not describe its provisions. The effective date 2025-12-16 is inferred from 'effective Tuesday' in a report dated Thursday 2025-12-18. A March 2026 report on a further chaplain memo (removing visible rank insignia, cutting faith codes) came from an aggregator and was dropped pending a reputable source. The Senate bill number and the House-passed FY2027 NDAA inclusion rest on the senator's release; the congress.gov bill pages could not be fetched. Whether the executive chaplain changes strengthen or reduce chaplain protections is characterized differently by supporters and critics; the record treats them as a parallel match. The senior-officer duty language was searched (the 2025-09-30 Quantico address and confirmation hearings) with no qualifying codification. The FY2026 NDAA was checked only through its table of contents (Sec. 504 on chaplain career flexibility).
